data.title: Azithromycin
data.summary: II Antibiotics — b) Macrolide · Azalide (15-membered macrolide)
data.body:
_Oral · II Antibiotics — b) Macrolide_

**Class:** Azalide (15-membered macrolide)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit (23S rRNA) and blocks translocation → stops protein synthesis
- Bacteriostatic; can be bactericidal at high concentrations
- Also anti-inflammatory (reduces neutrophil activity and cytokines)

## Pharmacokinetics
- Acid-stable; very high tissue and intracellular levels (concentrated in phagocytes, which carry it to infected sites)
- Very long tissue half-life (about 68 h) → single-dose or short-course regimens
- Mostly excreted unchanged in bile; little CYP3A4 inhibition (fewer interactions than erythromycin)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- STIs: chlamydia/NGU, chancroid, donovanosis, gonorrhoea (with ceftriaxone in some guidelines), early syphilis in special situations
- Skin and soft tissue infections; pyodermas in penicillin allergy
- Acne (pulse regimens) — used in India, but no better than doxycycline and promotes resistance
- Rosacea; trachoma; scrub typhus

## Dose & formulations
- Chlamydia/NGU: 1 g single dose
- Chancroid: 1 g single dose
- Donovanosis: 1 g once weekly, or 500 mg daily, for at least 3 weeks and until healed
- Early syphilis: 2 g single dose (resistance is common — penicillin remains first choice)
- Skin infection: 500 mg on day 1, then 250 mg daily on days 2–5
- Children: 10 mg/kg/day

## Adverse effects
- GI upset (less than erythromycin), diarrhoea
- QT prolongation and arrhythmia (caution in heart disease or with other QT drugs)
- Cholestatic hepatitis (rare), hearing loss with long high-dose courses
- Rash, rarely SJS/TEN; C. difficile colitis

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to macrolides
- History of cholestatic jaundice with azithromycin
- Caution: long QT, hypokalaemia, severe liver disease

## Drug interactions
- Other QT-prolonging drugs (fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics, hydroxychloroquine)
- Antacids reduce peak levels
- Warfarin and digoxin levels may rise (less than with erythromycin or clarithromycin)

## Monitoring
- None routinely; ECG if cardiac risk factors

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe in pregnancy (old FDA category B); used for chlamydia in pregnancy. Compatible with breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Long tissue half-life makes single-dose STI treatment possible
- Least CYP3A4 inhibition among macrolides
- Part of the NACO STI kits (e.g. kit 1 with cefixime) — check the slot-2 STI kits post
- Azithromycin-resistant Treponema pallidum is widespread, so it is not first-line for syphilis

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.9; Khopkar ch.1 (Macrolides). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
